newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to discuss Karachi rail project.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to discuss Karachi rail project.

text.p: Pakistani officials will discuss a proposed $586 million light rail project for the congested southern port city of Karachi with its sponsors next week, an industry source said on Friday.

An executive of the Indus Mass Transit Co Ltd (IMTC), the sponsor of the project, said the Canadian government and lenders from Japan, the United States and Saudi Arabia had recently renewed their commitments to finance the scheme.

He said the sponsors, including Canada's SNC-Lavalin, Turkish construction company Sezai Turkes Feyzi Akkaya Construction Company and Adcon Engineering of Pakistan, would meet officials of the federal and Sindh provincial governments in Islamabad and Karachi on March 28 and 29.
Talks would focus on government commitments to provide its share of the funds, as well as guarantees to senior lenders, to enable financing arrangements to be completed by June.
In the first phase of the Karachi mass transit project, 14 km (nine miles) of track and 14 stations are to be built from Karachi Port to Karimabad in District Central.
Trains will be able to cover the distance in 30 minutes and carry at least 20,000 passengers an hour. The system is designed to carry 130 million passengers annually by the year 2000.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, an enthusiastic supporter of major infrastructure schemes, pledged ahead of the February 3 elections to complete the Karachi mass transit project.
